chapters.title: What one request costs
chapters.dek: Before any box gets drawn: how a design session is run, where the milliseconds of a single request go, and the handful of numbers every estimate is built from.

chapters.title: Where the state lives
chapters.dek: The database is the part you cannot restart your way out of. Choosing one, indexing it, copying it, splitting it — and the race two requests run against the same row.

chapters.title: Taking work off the request path
chapters.dek: Caches, queues and push. The three ways to answer faster than the work actually takes, and the new bug each one introduces.

chapters.title: The network is not reliable
chapters.dek: Timeouts, retries, duplicates and crashes halfway through. The chapter that decides whether the system double-charges, double-sends or quietly loses an order — and the one most courses skip.

chapters.title: Services, APIs and the front door
chapters.dek: What it really costs to turn a function call into a network call, what an API promises, and the gateway that a security review will actually read.

chapters.title: Running it
chapters.dek: A design is only finished when someone can tell what it is doing at 3am, ship a change while it runs, and say what it costs.

chapters.title: Whole systems
chapters.dek: Four full designs, each using everything above: one built around reads, one around background work, one around correctness, and one around a component that is expensive and sometimes wrong.

lessons.title: Design is a loop, not a diagram
lessons.dek: Requirements, estimate, sketch, deep-dive, trade-offs — the five moves of every design session, run once end to end on a URL shortener so the shape is familiar before the hard parts arrive.

lessons.title: Where 200 milliseconds go
lessons.dek: DNS, TLS, load balancer, app server, database, back. One request traced hop by hop, with the time each hop actually takes and the two hops where almost all of it is spent.

lessons.title: Numbers you must be able to estimate
lessons.dek: Latency numbers every engineer should know, QPS from daily users, storage from row sizes, bandwidth from both. The back-of-envelope discipline that tells you which part of the design is the hard part.

lessons.title: Make the server forget
lessons.dek: The first real scaling move is to let any server answer any request. Stateless services, where the session went, what the load balancer actually does, and health checks that lie.

lessons.title: Nines, and what "consistent" actually means
lessons.dek: SLI, SLO, SLA and what 99.9% costs. Then the word consistent, which means three different things, and the theorem that says you cannot have all of them during a partition.

lessons.title: Choosing a database is choosing what it will be bad at
lessons.dek: Relational, document, key-value, wide-column, graph, search. Each one is a decision about which queries are cheap — and, more usefully, which ones you have just made impossible.

lessons.title: The index you forgot, and the query that took the site down
lessons.dek: B-trees and LSM trees, what an index costs on write, reading an EXPLAIN plan, the N+1 pattern, and the hot row that serialises every request behind it.

lessons.title: Two copies are never the same copy
lessons.dek: Leader and followers, synchronous against asynchronous replication, and replication lag — the reason a user can save something and then not see it. Read-your-writes, and what failover really loses.

lessons.title: Splitting the data, and the key you can never change
lessons.dek: When one machine is not enough: shard keys, consistent hashing, the hot partition that one big customer creates, and why a cross-shard query is a design smell, not a feature.

lessons.title: The last seat that two people both booked
lessons.dek: Two checkouts, one seat left, both pass the check. Isolation levels, lost updates and write skew, SELECT FOR UPDATE against optimistic versions — and the row that must be locked even when the framework says it is fine.

lessons.title: A cache is a bet about the future
lessons.dek: Browser, CDN, application, database — four places to keep a copy, one rule for when each is wrong. Invalidation, TTL, cache-aside against write-through, the stampede, and the key everybody wants at once.

lessons.title: Do it later: queues, workers and backpressure
lessons.dek: Answer now, work later. Message queues, worker pools, what at-least-once delivery does to your consumer, dead-letter queues, and the backpressure that stops a slow downstream from filling your memory.

lessons.title: Telling the user before they ask
lessons.dek: Polling, long polling, server-sent events, WebSockets. Which one a status page needs, which one a chat needs, and the pub/sub layer that makes any of them work across more than one server.

lessons.title: Timeouts, retries, and the storm they cause together
lessons.dek: A retry without a timeout waits forever; a retry without jitter arrives with everyone else's. Exponential backoff, circuit breakers, bulkheads, load shedding — and why the outage usually starts one layer below the one that fell over.

lessons.title: Exactly-once is a lie you can engineer around
lessons.dek: The network will deliver your message twice or not at all; there is no third option. Idempotency keys, the unique constraint that enforces them, the transactional outbox, and consumers that survive a replay.

lessons.title: Who is the leader, and how do you know they still are
lessons.dek: Leader election, leases, fencing tokens and the lock that expired while its holder was still working. Raft in one page, and the honest answer to when you need etcd or ZooKeeper — which is rarely.

lessons.title: A workflow that survives a crash halfway
lessons.dek: Reserve the seat, charge the card, send the ticket — and the process dies between step two and three. Sagas, compensation, orchestration against choreography, and the state machine that makes every step resumable.

lessons.title: Monolith first, and what the second service really costs
lessons.dek: A function call became a network call: it can now time out, be duplicated, or answer from stale data. Modular monoliths, service boundaries drawn along data ownership, and the two reasons to split that are actually good.

lessons.title: An API is a promise you cannot take back
lessons.dek: REST, gRPC and GraphQL for the three jobs they are each good at. Versioning, pagination that survives inserts, idempotency in the header, and webhooks — the API that calls the other way.

lessons.title: The front door: gateway, rate limits and who you are
lessons.dek: The API gateway, token-bucket rate limiting, OAuth2 and JWT without the folklore, TLS termination and where secrets live. The lesson a security questionnaire is secretly quoting from.

lessons.title: Events as the record, tables as the view
lessons.dek: Event-driven architecture, event sourcing against plain CRUD, change data capture, and what a Kafka partition actually guarantees. Then the section every event-sourcing article leaves out: when it is overkill.

lessons.title: Three signals, one question: what is it doing right now
lessons.dek: Logs, metrics and traces answer different questions and cost different amounts. Correlation IDs, cardinality, and alerts written from the SLO rather than from the CPU graph — so that a page means something.

lessons.title: Shipping while it runs
lessons.dek: Blue/green, canary, feature flags, and the schema change that has to work with both the old and the new code at once. Expand-and-contract migrations, and a rollback that is rehearsed rather than hoped for.

lessons.title: Regions, backups and the bill
lessons.dek: RPO and RTO as the two numbers a disaster plan is made of, what multi-region really buys, autoscaling that arrives late, managed against self-hosted — and cost as a design constraint rather than an afterthought.

lessons.title: Design a notification system
lessons.dek: Email, SMS, push and in-app, for millions of users, with retries that do not spam and preferences that are honoured. Fan-out, template rendering, provider failover and the dedup that stops the second SMS.

lessons.title: Design a news feed
lessons.dek: Fan-out on write against fan-out on read, the celebrity problem that breaks both, ranking, and the cache that holds every user's first page. The classic, because it forces every read-scaling decision at once.

lessons.title: Design a payment system with a ledger
lessons.dek: Idempotent API, a payment state machine, a double-entry ledger that is never edited in place, an outbox to the provider adapter, webhooks for the truth, and a nightly reconciliation that proves the books. The one where a bug is a loss, not a ticket.

lessons.title: Design a feature on top of an LLM
lessons.dek: Retrieval, a vector index, streaming tokens to the browser, a semantic cache, and a cost model where one request is a thousand times dearer than a database read. Guardrails and evals, because the model is a component that is wrong on purpose sometimes.
